title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The notes study a profinite group 𝔊 (in practice the profinite completion of SL(2,Z), written Ĝ_{1,1}^{+∧}, or quotients of it such as SL(2,Ẑ), PSL, SL(2,Z/3)). The group sits in an extension (31): 1 → 𝔊 → G_{ρ,σ} → Γ_{ρ,σ}, with a 'cyclotomic' character χ_Γ : Γ_{ρ,σ} → Ẑ^×. Here ρ is the elliptic element of order 6 (order 3 mod ±1) and σ the element of order 4 with σ² = −1, so σ^{-1} = −σ. On the previous page, Γ' = Ker(ε_3∘χ) and Γ'' = Ker(ε_2∘χ) are index-2 subgroups. ε_3 and ε_2 are the characters Ẑ^× → (Z/3)^× = ±1 and Ẑ^× → (Z/4)^× = ±1, i.e. the quadratic characters of Q(√−3) and Q(i). The implicit hypothesis is the 'inertia' property: every g ∈ G_{ρ,σ} sends ρ to a 𝔊-conjugate of ρ^{χ(g)}, and σ to a 𝔊-conjugate of σ^{χ(g)}.

This page. (32) defines Z_ρ and Z_σ as the centralizers of ρ and σ in G_{ρ,σ}. (33) defines δ_ρ, δ_σ as the restrictions of δ_G to them. The claim is that δ_ρ(Z_ρ) ⊇ Γ' and δ_σ(Z_σ) ⊇ Γ''.

Proof sketch:
- Since ρ has order 6 and ρ^λ depends only on λ mod 6, take g with ε_3χ(g) = 1. Then g ρ g^{-1} is 𝔊-conjugate to ρ. Correcting g by an element of 𝔊 gives a lift in Z_ρ, so Γ' ⊆ δ_ρ(Z_ρ).
- If ε_3χ(g) = −1, then g ρ g^{-1} ~ ρ^{-1}. So g can be corrected to centralize ρ iff ρ ~ ρ^{-1} in 𝔊.
- Hence δ_ρ(Z_ρ) = Γ' if ρ and ρ^{-1} are not conjugate in 𝔊, and equals all of Γ_{ρ,σ} otherwise. The same argument for σ with ε_2 (mod 4) gives the analogous statement for Z_σ.
- This is the Proposition stated cleanly on the next page.

The crossed-out part tests the condition on examples:
- He first asserts that in SL(2,Ẑ), σ is conjugate to −σ 'by Steinberg's theory', so δ_σ would be surjective. He then asks whether this persists in the universal SL(2,Z)^ = Ĝ_{1,1}^{+∧}.
- He strikes the whole passage. The margin rewrites the conditions, distinguishing SL(2,Ẑ) from SL(2,Ẑ)/(±1).
- Next page: he proves via SL(2,Z/3) that ρ and ρ^{-1} are never conjugate when 𝔊 surjects onto it. The equation c² + cd + d² = −1 has no solution mod 3.

Interpretation. Z_ρ and Z_σ play the role of decomposition groups at the stacky points j = 0 and j = 1728 of M_{1,1}. These points have automorphism groups μ_6 and μ_4, and the theorem says the Galois image there is cut out by Q(√−3), resp. Q(i), unless the torsion element is conjugate to its inverse.
errors: The struck-out claim that σ is conjugate to −σ = σ^{-1} in SL(2,Ẑ) is false. In GL_2, the elements conjugating σ to σ^{-1} have the form f·τ with τ = diag(1,−1) and f = a + bσ, so one needs a² + b² = −1. This has no solution mod 4, hence none in Z_2, so σ and σ^{-1} are not conjugate in SL(2,Z_2), nor in SL(2,Ẑ). It becomes true only mod ±1, where σ is an involution. Grothendieck crossed the passage out, and the margin note specifying SL(2,Ẑ)(±1) appears to be the correction.
Minor: the mod-4 character is called ε_2 (indexed by the prime 2, though it is the character mod 4). That is a naming convention, not an error.

ideas.what: Image of the centralizer of a torsion element in an extension of a 'Galois' group by a profinite group. It contains the kernel of the relevant quadratic character and is everything iff the torsion element is conjugate to its inverse.
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on stack inertia / decomposition groups at points with extra automorphisms (elliptic points j=0, 1728 of M_{1,1}); 'I-type' / cyclotomic action on torsion of profinite mapping class groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Collas, Collas–Maugeais (2010s), building on Ihara–Nakamura-type studies of the Galois action on Teichmüller groups
ideas.where_published: Lochak–Schneps 'Esquisse' circle mentions special points; La Longue Marche discusses the modular tower; unsure about this exact statement

ideas.what: Using finite quotients (SL(2,Z/3), mod 4) to detect non-conjugacy of ρ and ρ^{-1} (resp. σ and σ^{-1}) in the profinite completion, via norm equations c²+cd+d² = −1 mod 3 and a²+b² = −1 mod 4.
ideas.modern_name: local obstruction to real/rational conjugacy of torsion elements (norm forms of Z[ω], Z[i])

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly sets up the Galois image at the elliptic points of M_{1,1} as the image of centralizers of torsion elements in an extension of Γ by SL(2,Z)^. He identifies it with Ker of the Q(√−3) / Q(i) characters, conditioned on conjugacy of ρ, σ with their inverses. This anticipates the later 'Galois action on stack inertia' programme (Collas–Maugeais) in the special case of genus 1.
missed.quote: Z_ρ = Centr_{G_{ρ,σ}}(ρ) ... ont des images qui contiennent Γ'_{ρ,σ} et Γ''_{ρ,σ} respectivement
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority only. The result itself is elementary and essentially consistent with later published work on cyclotomic action on torsion in profinite mapping class groups.

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary but well-aimed group theory, anticipating later work on Galois action at stacky points of M_{1,1}. The content is routine, and the one substantive claim on this page (σ ~ −σ in SL(2,Ẑ)) is wrong and was crossed out.
transcription_corrections: 'γ_{ρ,σ}', 'γ'_{ρ,σ}', 'γ''_{ρ,σ}' should read Γ_{ρ,σ}, Γ'_{ρ,σ}, Γ''_{ρ,σ} (as on the previous page).
'Ĝ' in the struck passage is the fraktur 𝔊 (the profinite group), as on the next page.
Line 3 reads 'alors les homom. induits par δ_G'.
The struck parenthetical seems to be '(ou égale) ssi ρ et ρ^{-1} non conjugués dans 𝔊', matching the Proposition on the next page.
The struck SL(2,Ẑ) passage contains 'σ y est conjugué à −σ, par la théorie de Steinberg p. ex.' and ends with 'la condition le serait-il encore dans le universel SL(2,Z)^ = 𝔊_{1,1}^{+∧} ?'.
